brief: BofA's Subramanian argues investors should stop waiting for a "clearing event" to deliver market clarity, since 2026's biggest IPO, Q3 earnings reactions, and recent policy surprises each failed to produce lasting direction; the team recommends implementing now through standalone screens instead of waiting. On AI, no single narrative holds: semis are raising capex, hyperscalers are vertically integrating, and even non-AI firms like IT services see rising demand for AI expertise; the AI GARP screen favors AI-linked names with cash-backed earnings because AI-driven capex is pressuring free-cash-flow-to-earnings conversion market-wide. Diversification is scarce: gold has moved into positive co-movement with equities since March, bonds and stocks historically turn positively correlated once 10-year yields clear 6%, negative-beta S&P 500 stocks sit at record highs, and high-dividend-yield stocks have been more negatively correlated with the S&P 500 than gold, bonds, real estate, or alternatives in 34 of the past 40 years. A value tilt is working (Value +7% MTD vs. Growth -2%, Momentum -5%, led by FCF/EV), though BofA expects GARP to win if profits slow. The document is otherwise a set of quant screens explicitly disclaimed as not recommended lists.
